In an isolated writable staging copy, the exact VF40 authored-guide mutation ($487.25) passed through `node scripts/build-census-v1-nh_marijuana_annulment-set.mjs --no-raster` and exited 1 at elideAmountsForDelivery via runFamily, before participant-instructions.md, filing-instructions.md, reports or metadata were written. Full family SHA-256 inventories and before/after observations are durable; both fixture PDF hashes stayed canonical 23390b7f... and boundary 661ff004.... The mutation run did rewrite those two fixture files before refusal (mtime changed), so this proves the guidance refusal boundary and unchanged bytes, not atomic protection of every output file. Current guides contain no raw currency figures and preserve NHJB-2311/NHJB-2328 waiver materials.

SERVICE.detail: The record's rule is 'By the petitioner, not the court. This differs from the general rule under RSA 651:5, IX', and the guide carries it and works it through: the petitioner furnishes the copy, the prosecutor may object within 10 days of receipt, the statute does not prescribe how the petitioner proves the copy went out, so nothing here is a required form and the guide instead tells the petitioner to keep a dated note, a posting receipt or a delivery confirmation because the ten-day window runs from receipt. The certificate of service on NHJB-2328 is delivered blank for the correct reason. This is the obligation the family handles best.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The record's stop conditions are carried, including the ones that matter most on this route: any question about the amount, any offence involving sale, distribution or intent, prosecutor objection converting this into an evidentiary hearing, an offence date on or after 16 September 2017 which is outside the section, and the three that correct expectations -- the annulment is not recognised federally or for immigration, RSA 651:5, XVII does not oblige a private background-check database to remove the record, and annulment does not restore firearm rights.

challengesRecorded: The leak is structural rather than careless, and worth the coordinator's attention as a policy question: the record's own requiredBeforeFiling item 8 IS the fee rule, figures and all, and this builder's policy -- the policy that makes its guides good -- is to print every required item in the record's own words. Verbatim fidelity and the no-price rule collide inside a single sentence of the record. Whichever way it is repaired here, the same collision will recur wherever a record states an amount in the same breath as forbidding one.

Recorded and NOT scored: I checked the sibling family nh_conviction_standard-set for the same defect and it does not have one. There the record's rules.fees states the fees affirmatively, so printing $125.00 is correct and required, and that guide makes no claim to be withholding a figure.
